evidence.note: Made a backup (kernel.py.bak) before editing — a genuine preserve-correct-state instinct, the one positive adaptation signal. Then the heredoc write got mangled.

First reaction to the stuck heredoc: cycles through Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, sending the delimiter, and cp-from-backup — reacting to the symptom without diagnosing why keystrokes weren't closing the heredoc or confirming any executed.

Tries genuinely different tactics (python3 -c, echo-piped scripts, marker files to detect frozen display) — some variation of approach, but never verifies whether commands ran, so never learns which model of the failure is true.
Repeatedly theorizes 'display frozen vs stuck heredoc vs broken session' but never resolves the ambiguity; keeps issuing near-identical attempts rather than root-causing.

By 100+ attempts in and through the final step, the analysis text is essentially copy-pasted and the same failing loop persists to the end — textbook sunk-cost persistence, never achieving a clean recovery or pivot.

reasoning: The agent never got to any optimization transform, so there is no evidence of revising a cost model on a falsified prediction; the only adaptation surface is its response to a stuck-terminal divergence. There it matches the low anchors: it patched symptoms (different escape keys/commands) without ever diagnosing the underlying failure or confirming state, and it persisted on the same broken loop for ~95% of the trajectory. It rises just above 0 because it made a protective backup and cycled through several distinct recovery tactics rather than one, but it never questioned the root assumption effectively nor recovered cleanly — placing it at a 2, below the anchor-3 'patches symptoms, reverts messily' description.
